tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.text:
I've now cross-checked the plan against the actual branch commits and the live Jira statuses. Here's the evaluation.

## The one thing that gates everything

**Master is still at `de32631` — PR #52 (PR 1) has not merged.** Every other branch is physically stacked on top of PR 1's 28 commits:

- PR 2 branch = PR 1 (28) + W4 + W5 → 59 commits
- PR 3 branch = PR 1 + W4 + W5 group A + W6 + W7 → 61 commits

So none of PR 2–5 can be opened as a clean PR against `master` until PR 1 lands. The fastest thing you can do for the SW-589 deadline (which passed on 2026-11-24 — the ticket is now overdue) is **get Gilad and Avichai to review and merge PR #52.** That unblocks the rest of the chain.

## Readiness by PR

| PR | Workstreams | Jira | Code state | Can open? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **PR 1** (#52, pushed) | W0–W3 + G22 + G26 | SW-594/595/596 **Done** | Complete | **Already open. Just needs review + merge.** |
| **PR 2** `preprocess-features` | W4, W5 | SW-597, SW-598 **In Progress** | Code-complete except G10, G20 | **Yes, after de-scoping G10 + G20** |
| **PR 3** `training-defaults` | W6, W7, G3, G9 | SW-599, SW-600 **Done** | Carries metric-changing items tied to SW-606 (ON HOLD) | **Hold, or split** |
| **PR 4** reports | W8 | SW-601 **To Do** | Not started | No |
| **PR 5** stages/tools | W9 | SW-602 **To Do** | Not started | No |

## What is missing in each, and my recommendation

**PR 1 — ready.** G3/G9 are already carved out (SW-606, Eran) and recorded as WAITING in the findings. Nothing blocks it. Action: chase the two required reviewers.

**PR 2 — open it, after carving out two items.** Everything is committed and tested (W4 A/B, W5 A/B including M4/M5/L14 as byte-identical opt-ins, G11, H5). The genuinely unfinished pieces are:
- **G10 + H4 wiring** — Eran's `eran_preprocess.py` is on master but still not called from the stage; it needs Eran's confirmation of which version is final. This is the one real code gap.
- **G20** — missing-value policy; Eran deferred it to Gilad and Avichai. Still BLOCKED.
- Confirmation-only (code already committed, won't change unless the answer differs): M6 valid-only pool + before/after median, M7 layout file format (Eran); G11 `blip_tuple` dataset check (Avichai).

Recommendation: log **G10 and G20 as their own tickets**, mark both WAITING in the findings, and open PR 2 without them. Keep M6/M7/G11 in PR 2 as-is with the open confirmations noted — they don't hold the code back.

**Before opening PR 2, clean up the branch sprawl.** W5 group B now exists on `preprocess-features`, on the current `feature-selection` branch, and `tram/sw-589-preprocessing` holds yet another copy of the G11 commits — all with different hashes. Pick one branch as PR 2 and delete the others, or you'll get a messy merge.

**PR 3 — hold or split.** W6 and W7 group A are clean and approved. But the branch also now carries the metric-changing work: W7 group B (M12, M13, L15 — Optuna scripts removed, xgboost pinned) and the G9 "default per-trace runs to the adapted models" commit. Two problems:
- **G3 depends on SW-606, which is ON HOLD** (the defaults meeting).
- Your 2026-11-25 daily report still lists M12/M13/L15 and the adapted-model default as blockers waiting on Gilad/Eran/Avichai — yet **SW-600 (W7) is marked Done** and those commits are already on the branch. That mismatch needs resolving before this opens: either the sign-offs happened (then confirm and open), or they didn't (then those commits are ahead of approval).

Recommendation: split PR 3 into the no-change part (W6 + W7 group A + G9 provenance) which can open with PR 2, and move G3 (SW-606) and any unsigned metric-changing item to their own tickets/PR.

**PR 4 and PR 5 — de-scope from SW-589.** These are the bulk of what won't make the deadline. SW-601 (W8) and SW-602 (W9) already exist as subtasks; SW-604 and SW-605 (both To Do, yours) are folded into W8. To protect the deadline, treat W8 and W9 as follow-on work that closes under their own tickets, not under SW-589.

## Tickets to log so they don't hold up SW-589

Already exist (just keep them out of the SW-589 critical path): **SW-606** (G3 defaults, ON HOLD), **SW-601** (W8), **SW-602** (W9), **SW-604**, **SW-605**, **SW-607**, **SW-610**, **SW-611**.

New ones worth creating:
- **G10** — wire `eran_preprocess.py` into the preprocessing stage; owner Eran (blocks only the last slice of W4).
- **G20** — missing-value fill policy for selection vs. training; owner Gilad + Avichai.
- Optionally one ticket for the **W7 group B metric decisions** if they turn out not to be signed off.

## Bottom line

You can open **three PRs now** without waiting on anyone: PR 1 (already #52), PR 2 (after carving G10/G20 and cleaning the branches), and a trimmed no-change PR 3 (W6 + W7 group A + G9 provenance). Everything cross-team or metric-changing — G10, G20, G3/SW-606, the W7-B decisions, W8, W9 — gets logged as its own ticket and drops off SW-589's path. Once the three clean PRs merge, SW-589 can close with the remainder tracked independently.

Two things I'd confirm before acting: **(1)** is PR #52 actually in review, or stuck waiting on you to request reviewers? **(2)** were the W7 group B / adapted-model decisions signed off — since the commits are on the branch and SW-600 is Done, but your last daily report still lists them as open?

Want me to save this as `.claude.local/reviews/pr_readiness_SW-589.md`, or draft the G10 and G20 tickets for your review?

content.text:
Here's the verdict.

## PR 1's approval is not the blocker — you can work around it

A PR 2 to `master` would show reviewers **61 commits** (all 28 of PR 1 re-included + your 33 of new work). That's the wrong thing to open, and it couldn't merge without pulling PR 1's content in behind its back.

The right move is a **stacked PR: target PR 2 at `tram/sw-589-pr38-findings`, not `master`.** Bitbucket lets you pick the destination branch. Then the PR shows only the **33 commits** of actual W4 + W5 + H5 work, reviewers (Gilad, Avichai, Eran) can start now in parallel with PR 1, and when PR 1 merges you retarget PR 2 to `master` (it rebases automatically). The one hard rule stays: **don't merge PR 2 before PR 1.**

So yes, you don't have to wait on PR 1. But two things make it *not quite ready* regardless:

## Gap 1 — two in-scope findings are still open on the branch

- **G10** — still `ACCEPTED`, "module on master, not wired". Eran's `eran_preprocess.py` is not called from the stage; waiting on which version is final.
- **G20** — still `ACCEPTED`, "open". Missing-value fill policy; Eran deferred it to Gilad and Avichai.

Opening PR 2 with two unresolved ACCEPTED items in its findings file is exactly what you wanted to avoid for the deadline. Carve both into their own tickets (G10 → Eran, G20 → Gilad + Avichai), flip them to `WAITING (owner, SW-xxx)` in the findings file, and they drop off PR 2's critical path. This is the "log as independent tickets" step from our earlier plan.

content.content:
=== G20 section ===
### G20

**Status:** ACCEPTED · **Verified:** yes

**Resolution:** W0: open; `impute_with_selector` at `feature_extraction.py:2468` → W5.

**Where:** `src/core/feature_extraction.py (impute_with_selector, fit_selector, RobustFeatureSelector._clean_features), src/core/feature_selection_poolsel.py (clean_matrix, clean_feature_frame), src/core/stages/features.py:747-827, src/core/stages/holdout.py:1025-1058`

Review `impute_with_selector` and its effect on feature selection. It does not change which features are chosen. `select_features` (holdout: `_select_holdout_features`) finishes first; `fit_selector(..., feature_names=selected)` only stores medians; `impute_with_selector` then `fillna`s the train, test, and estimation frames. The effect is that selection scores one fill and the model trains on another. Ensemble and the other rankers run `_clean_features` on a copy: median when a column is under 10% missing, 0 otherwise. `patient_mrmr_consensus` skips that call, but poolsel's `clean_matrix` fills every NaN with 0 before scoring, and `clean_feature_frame` uses the same 10% rule before the redundancy step. That copy is thrown away. The medians written onto `FeatureSelectorState` are the raw training-column medians (NaNs skipped), and `impute_with_selector` applies that median to every selected column, including columns selection filled with 0. A feature can win the funnel on zero-filled values and then be fit on median-filled values. The medians are taken on the whole train+validation pool, so the later validation split is filled with constants that validation rows helped set. The blind test and the estimation set do not contribute, which is correct. A selected column that is entirely NaN stores `nan`, and `fillna` leaves it missing, so Easy Ensemble still sees the NaN it was meant to remove. Make the matrix that is scored and the matrix that is trained the same fill, or record the difference as intentional.

### G21
